title: Minimum Cost to Convert String I
summary: Given two strings of equal length, source and target, and arrays for original, changed characters, and their conversion costs, determine the minimum cost to convert source into target.
statement: Given two strings of equal length, source and target, and arrays for original, changed characters, and their conversion costs, determine the minimum cost to convert source into target. Operations involve changing a character in source to a corresponding character in target at specified costs. If conversion is impossible, return -1.
constraints: source and target are equal-length lowercase strings.
Each listed directed character conversion may be used any number of times; duplicate rules may have different costs.
Return the minimum total position-wise conversion cost, or -1 if any position is unreachable.
hints: Character rules form a directed weighted graph shared by every string position.
Compute all-pairs shortest paths once, then sum the required distance for each aligned character pair.
Initialize direct minima and zero diagonals; run Floyd–Warshall; reject infinity while scanning source and target.
Every sequence of character changes is a graph path, and Floyd–Warshall finds its minimum cost; positions are independent, so their minima add.
editorial: Every sequence of character changes is a graph path, and Floyd–Warshall finds its minimum cost; positions are independent, so their minima add.

tests.explanation: The cheapest position costs are zero, five, three through c→e→b, and twenty, totaling twenty-eight.
Each a follows the two-edge path a→c→b for three, so four positions cost twelve.
